name: Ötztaler Heimat- und Freilichtmuseum Längenfeld
kurzbeschreibung: The Ötztaler Heimat- und Freilichtmuseum in Längenfeld-Lehn: 15 historic buildings from the 17th to the 20th century showcase alpine mountain farming culture.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Ötztaler Heimat- und Freilichtmuseum is situated in the idyllic hamlet of Lehn in the municipality of Längenfeld in central Ötztal (Imst district) at an elevation of around 1,180 metres. Surrounded by the steep mountain flanks of the Stubaier Alpen and Ötztaler Alpen, the heritage-listed complex forms one of western Austria's most significant regional open-air museums. Across spacious meadow grounds, the museum gathers 15 historic original buildings spanning four centuries, vividly bringing to life the arduous, frugal working and living conditions of the Ötztal mountain farming community before the advent of modern alpine tourism.

Open-Air Ensemble & Flax Cultivation

The roots of the museum date back to 1971, when dedicated local heritage researchers rescued a Paarhof farmstead threatened with decay and carefully relocated it to Lehn. The centerpiece of the ensemble is the imposing 17th-century Haupthaus with its wood-panelled smoke kitchen, traditional parlor featuring a masonry rear-loaded tiled stove, and sparse sleeping quarters. Grouped around the farmhouse are fully functional agricultural and trade outbuildings: a monumental granary, a water-powered grain mill, a sawmill, a baking oven, a sheep wool processing workshop, and a historic wooden clog maker's workshop. A special focus of the museum highlights the centuries-old, vital practice of Ötztaler Flachsanbau (flax cultivation): from the sowing of flax seeds through rippling, breaking, and hackling to weaving on ancient handlooms, the painstaking production of the famed Ötztaler Bauernleinen (farm linen) is thoroughly documented. A historic cottage garden with traditional heritage varieties of vegetables and medicinal herbs adapted to the harsh high-alpine climate completes the open-air cultural site.

Visit & Getting There

The Ötztaler Heimat- und Freilichtmuseum is open during the summer season from early June to early October: Tuesday to Friday from 10:00 to 17:00, and Sundays from 14:00 to 17:00 (closed on Mondays and Saturdays; special group tours available on request outside regular hours). Admission prices (as of the 2025/2026 season): adults approx. €7.00, seniors approx. €6.00, children and youths (aged 6 to 15) approx. €3.50, young children under 6 free; family ticket approx. €16.00. Holders of the regional Ötztal Inside Summer Card enjoy free admission! Arrival by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Ötztal), continue along the Ötztalstraße B186 approximately 25 km into the valley to Längenfeld, and in the hamlet of Lehn follow the signs to the museum (free parking directly at the entrance, Lehn 24). By public transport: ÖBB trains to Bahnhof Ötztal, where VVT bus line 4194 runs every 30 minutes directly to the stop Längenfeld Lehn (only about a three-minute walk from there).

Tips

The outdoor grounds are level and paved with well-maintained meadow and gravel paths, making them easily accessible for strollers and all-terrain wheelchairs (occasional low wooden thresholds lead into the historic rooms). Every Wednesday morning in July and August, demonstrations of the historic baking oven and traditional crafts take place, where freshly baked farmhouse bread can be sampled. Combine your museum visit with a scenic hike to the nearby Lehnbachfall waterfall.
